newsitem.title: ZAMBIA: ZAMBIA SELLS STAKES IN BP , AGIP PETROLI.
newsitem.headline: ZAMBIA SELLS STAKES IN BP , AGIP PETROLI.

text.p: The Zambian government has sold its shareholdings in British Petroleum Zambia Ltd and Agip Zambia Ltd to BP Africa and Agip Petroli International BV respectively, the Zambia Privatisation Agency (ZPA) said on Tuesday.

"The ZPA is pleased to announce the sale of government's 25 percent shareholding to BP Africa...and the sale of its 50 percent shareholding in Agip Zambia to Agip Petroli following the successful completion of negotiations," ZPA chief executive Valentine Chiatalu told a news conference.
Government shares in the BP unit were sold for $3.3 million of which $0.3 million had already been paid as a deposit. Agip Zambia shares were sold for $850,000.
Meanwhile, Chiatalu said 137 of the 271 state-run companies and units earmarked for privatisation had been sold since the programme started three years ago.
The ZPA expected to realise at least $20 million in sales of state-run enterprises this year.
